options.a: Inheritance
options.b: Homestead
options.c: Reversion
options.d: Survivorship

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses joint tenancy with tenancy in common; a joint tenant's interest passes to co-owners, not heirs.
distractorExplanations.b: Homestead is a separate protection of a residence from certain creditors, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.c: Reversion is the grantor's future interest after a life estate, unrelated to co-ownership rights.

options.a: Obtain the highest possible price even when the seller directs a quicker sale
options.b: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
options.c: Treat buyer and seller with equal advocacy so both receive fair representation
options.d: Advise the seller on title and tax matters as the seller's legal representative

distractorExplanations.a: Price is not the top duty; obedience requires following the seller's lawful instruction to favor a quick sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal advocacy describes a neutral or dual role; a listing broker owes loyalty to the seller client, not both sides.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses agency with legal practice; a broker must refer title and tax questions to an attorney or CPA.

options.a: At closing, when the settlement agent reviews the final agency paperwork
options.b: Once the purchase contract is accepted and both parties have signed it
options.c: Only if one of the parties is an existing client rather than a customer
options.d: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises

distractorExplanations.a: Closing is far too late; informed consent must come before the licensee acts for both parties.
distractorExplanations.b: Waiting until acceptance means both parties negotiated without knowing the licensee's divided loyalty.
distractorExplanations.c: Disclosure is triggered by the dual or designated relationship itself, not by whether a party was a prior client.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated. Exact timing follows the applicable license-law rules.

options.a: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.b: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.c: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.b: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: The seller's reason for selling and lowest acceptable price, even if the seller objects
options.b: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.c: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood, since it may affect desirability
options.d: Obvious patent defects, while hidden latent defects are left for the buyer's own inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts a buyer must be told.
distractorExplanations.c: Commenting on a neighborhood's race or religion is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required material-fact disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: known latent (hidden) defects are exactly what must be disclosed, because a buyer cannot readily discover them.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared, as required by law; confidential motivations may be protected.

options.a: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.b: Parties may still perform within a reasonable time after each stated deadline passes
options.c: The closing date is firm, but other contingency deadlines may slip
options.d: The offer expires if the seller does not accept it within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.b: That is the default rule when the clause is absent; time is of the essence makes the stated deadlines strictly enforceable.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause applies to all contract dates, including inspection, financing, and appraisal contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the clause with an offer's expiration term; time is of the essence governs performance deadlines in the contract.

options.a: The broker's compensation is a fixed percentage of the final sale price
options.b: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.c: The seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission
options.d: The broker's flat fee is owed up front even if the property does not sell

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a standard percentage commission listing, which does not create the net listing's incentive to underprice.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an exclusive agency listing, not a net listing where the broker keeps everything above the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a net listing with a flat-fee or advance-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker only the excess over the net price.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings pay the broker the amount above the seller's net price, creating conflict-of-interest concerns: they can incentivize underpricing and are banned or tightly regulated in many places.

options.a: Public use and the owner's consent
options.b: Payment of the property's assessed value
options.c: A police-power finding without compensation
options.d: Public use/purpose and just compensation

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; the owner's consent is not required, which is what distinguishes condemnation from a voluntary sale.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation is based on fair market value, not the tax assessor's assessed value, which is often lower.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses eminent domain with police power: zoning and code regulation need no compensation, but a taking does.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public use/purpose and just compensation under the Fifth Amendment (constitutional framework).

options.a: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability
options.b: A zoning variance granted to the owner for a hardship use
options.c: A deed recorded with a full covenant of warranty from the grantor
options.d: The abstract summary of the chain of title prepared for a buyer

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses public land-use control with title: a variance governs permitted use and is not a claim against ownership.
distractorExplanations.c: A recorded general warranty deed strengthens the chain of title; it is the opposite of a cloud that casts doubt on it.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses an abstract of title (a history of recorded documents) with a cloud, which is a defect or claim the abstract may reveal.

options.a: Must acquire title at the same time and by the same deed as each other
options.b: Hold equal undivided shares, and a deceased owner's share passes to the others
options.c: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.d: Cannot sell or will their share without the other co-owners' consent

distractorExplanations.a: Unity of time and title are joint tenancy requirements; tenants in common may acquire their shares at different times by different deeds.
distractorExplanations.b: Equal shares plus right of survivorship are joint tenancy features; a tenant in common's share passes to heirs or devisees.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may freely sell, mortgage, or will an undivided share without the other co-owners' consent.

options.a: 1% of the loan amount
options.b: 1% of the purchase price
options.c: 1% of the down payment
options.d: 1% of the interest rate

distractorExplanations.b: Points are computed on the loan amount, not the price; on a $200,000 price with a $160,000 loan, one point is $1,600.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses the wrong base: the down payment is the buyer's equity, while points are a percentage of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses one point (1% of the loan amount) with one percentage point of interest rate; a point typically buys down far less.

options.a: Can adjust whenever the lender chooses, without caps
options.b: Adjusts with the margin while the index stays fixed
options.c: Changes only when the borrower refinances the loan
options.d: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps

distractorExplanations.a: ARM changes follow a published index on set adjustment dates, and periodic and lifetime caps limit each change.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the terms: the margin is fixed for the loan's life, and the index is the variable part that moves.
distractorExplanations.c: A refinance replaces the loan with a new note; an ARM's rate resets on scheduled adjustment dates under the existing note.

options.a: Physical damage to the home from fire, wind, or other covered perils
options.b: Covered title defects and claims against ownership per the policy
options.c: Losses to the lender when the borrower defaults on the mortgage
options.d: Title defects that arise after the policy date from future owners' acts

distractorExplanations.a: That is hazard (homeowners) insurance; title insurance covers defects in ownership, not physical damage to the structure.
distractorExplanations.c: That is mortgage insurance (PMI or FHA MIP); a lender's title policy protects the lien's validity, not repayment.
distractorExplanations.d: Title insurance looks backward: it covers defects existing on the policy date, not problems created by later owners.

options.a: Maximum loan-to-value ratios that lenders may offer on certain loans
options.b: Minimum disclosures of APR and finance charges on consumer loans
options.c: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.d: Maximum property tax rates that local governments may levy

distractorExplanations.a: LTV limits come from lender and investor underwriting guidelines, not usury laws, which cap the interest rate charged.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), which requires cost disclosure but does not cap interest rates.
distractorExplanations.d: Property tax limits are set by tax and levy laws; usury laws apply to interest charged by lenders on loans.

options.a: The seller owes no commission if the seller personally finds the buyer, but owes one if any broker does
options.b: The commission goes to whichever broker procures the buyer, as with an open listing given to several firms
options.c: The listing broker earns a commission only for sales that close in a protection period after the listing expires
options.d: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer

distractorExplanations.a: Describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell commission-free; exclusive right-to-sell removes that exception.
distractorExplanations.b: Describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid; exclusive right-to-sell pays the listing broker on any sale.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses the carryover (protection) clause after expiration with the core right-to-sell protection during the listing term.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term. The commission terms come from the signed listing agreement.

options.a: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.b: Suggest an offer figure, since giving price advice to a customer creates no agency duty
options.c: Disclose the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can make a realistic offer
options.d: Refer the buyer to the seller to negotiate the offer price directly with no agent

distractorExplanations.b: Wrong: advising a buyer on offer price is advocacy against the seller client and can create an undisclosed agency relationship.
distractorExplanations.c: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality and loyalty owed to the listing client.
distractorExplanations.d: Sidesteps the listing agent's duty to the seller and does not resolve the advocacy issue; the agent stays in the seller's role.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If the law and brokerage policy allow, buyer agency must be properly created and disclosed before advocating for the buyer.

options.a: Signed under a mistaken belief about the market value
options.b: Later found a better-priced property elsewhere
options.c: Changed their mind before closing
options.d: Was induced by fraud or was a minor

distractorExplanations.a: A one-sided mistake about value or a bad bargain does not make a contract voidable; fraud or incapacity does.
distractorExplanations.b: Buyer's remorse over a better deal is not a legal ground to void a contract; that would be a breach.
distractorExplanations.c: Changing one's mind after a binding contract is formed is a breach, not a ground that makes the contract voidable.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether a particular contract is voidable depends on the circumstances and state law.

options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms within a period
options.b: A right of first refusal to match any later third-party offer
options.c: Equitable title to the property as soon as the option is signed
options.d: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the duty: the optionee holds a right, not an obligation; only the optionor is bound (to sell if exercised).
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses an option (fixed price and terms) with a right of first refusal, which only lets the holder match another offer.
distractorExplanations.c: Equitable title passes under a sales contract once a binding purchase exists; an unexercised option gives no title interest.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: An option is a purchased right, not an obligation, to buy on fixed terms for a time. The optionor is usually paid consideration for keeping the offer open.

options.a: A misstatement of a measurable fact, such as lot size, that buyers may rely upon
options.b: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.c: An implied warranty of quality that binds the seller once the buyer relies on it
options.d: A form of negligent misrepresentation that licensees are liable for if a buyer relies on it

distractorExplanations.a: That is misrepresentation; puffing is vague opinion, while measurable facts like lot size must be accurate.
distractorExplanations.c: Puffing creates no warranty; a reasonable buyer is not expected to treat sales talk as a promise of quality.
distractorExplanations.d: Negligent misrepresentation involves a false statement of fact; opinion-level puffing is not actionable on its own.

options.a: Practicing law when filling in any blank on a preprinted purchase form
options.b: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.c: Required to have an attorney review every completed form before signing
options.d: Free to add custom legal clauses if the client asks for them in writing

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in blanks on approved forms is generally permitted; the line is drafting new legal clauses.
distractorExplanations.c: No general rule requires attorney review of every standard form; licensees may complete approved forms.
distractorExplanations.d: A client's request does not authorize a licensee to draft legal language; that is still unauthorized practice of law.

options.a: Proceed as a dual agent and give the seller a written dual agency disclosure after the offer is signed
options.b: Act as dual agent if the buyer consents in writing, since one party's consent suffices
options.c: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.d: Treat the buyer as a client and the seller as a customer without telling the seller

distractorExplanations.a: Disclosure after the fact is not informed consent; dual agency needs the client's written consent before it begins.
distractorExplanations.b: Dual agency requires informed written consent from both clients, not just the buyer.
distractorExplanations.d: Secretly downgrading an existing client to customer status is undisclosed dual agency and a loyalty breach.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Consent is required for dual agency where the model is used; without it, other compliant paths are needed. The broker chooses whichever compliant path fits the situation.

options.a: Spending client trust money on the broker's own business expenses
options.b: Holding earnest money for several different clients in one pooled trust account
options.c: Depositing earnest money after the legally required deadline
options.d: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly

distractorExplanations.a: That is conversion (using trust money for oneself); commingling is the mixing of funds, even if none is spent.
distractorExplanations.b: A pooled trust account for multiple clients with proper ledgers is permitted; commingling is mixing trust and broker money.
distractorExplanations.c: A late deposit violates the deposit timeline rule, not the commingling rule against mixing trust and personal funds.

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: When the life tenant conveys the property
options.c: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.d: After the statutory 99-year maximum term

distractorExplanations.a: The remainderman's death does not end the life estate; the remainder interest simply passes to the remainderman's heirs.
distractorExplanations.b: A life tenant may convey the interest, but the buyer receives an estate pur autre vie that still ends at the original life tenant's death.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a life estate with a long-term ground lease; a life estate is measured by a life, not a fixed term of years.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; remainder/reversion follows. The estate may also be measured by another person's life (pur autre vie).

options.a: A rezoning that changes the permitted use for an entire district
options.b: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.c: A use that was lawful before the zoning changed and may continue
options.d: A special-use permit allowed in the zone if listed conditions are met

distractorExplanations.a: That is a zoning amendment (map change); a variance gives one parcel relief without rezoning the district.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes a legal nonconforming use (grandfathered use), not a variance granted for hardship.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a variance with a conditional or special-use permit, which the ordinance already allows if conditions are met.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. The variance is granted by the zoning authority, such as a zoning board of appeals.

options.a: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.b: Having the grantor's signature notarized
options.c: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.d: Taking open physical possession of the land

distractorExplanations.a: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties but give no notice to the world; recording does.
distractorExplanations.b: Acknowledgment (notarization) usually makes a deed eligible for recording but does not itself give constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Possession gives inquiry (actual) notice to those who inspect, not the constructive notice created by recording.

options.a: Land bordering a lake, sea, or ocean shoreline
options.b: Rights to groundwater beneath the land surface
options.c: Water rights allocated by priority of first beneficial use
options.d: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream

distractorExplanations.a: Land on lakes, seas, and oceans involves littoral rights; riparian rights concern flowing water such as rivers.
distractorExplanations.b: Groundwater (percolating water) is governed by separate rules; riparian rights attach to land along flowing surface water.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes the prior appropriation doctrine used in many western states, which is the alternative to riparian rights.

options.a: Interest alone, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.b: Principal first, with interest deferred and added to the loan balance
options.c: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.d: Interest and escrow items, with principal paid off at the end

distractorExplanations.a: Describes an interest-only or balloon loan; a fully amortizing payment reduces principal with every installment.
distractorExplanations.b: Deferred interest added to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of an amortizing loan.
distractorExplanations.d: Paying principal only at the end is a term (straight) loan; amortization pays principal down throughout the term.

options.a: Requiring disclosure of the APR and finance charge before consummation
options.b: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.c: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures
options.d: Requiring lenders to report home loan data by census tract

distractorExplanations.a: APR and finance-charge disclosure is the core of the Truth in Lending Act (TILA), not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.b: Credit discrimination based on protected traits is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA), not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.d: Reporting loan data by geography is the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA), not RESPA.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-m.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures (with TRID integration for many loans). RESPA applies to covered federally related mortgage transactions.

options.a: Lets the lender call the full balance due if the property is sold
options.b: Adds a late charge when a payment arrives after the grace period
options.c: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early
options.d: Charges a fee to assume the existing loan

distractorExplanations.a: Describes a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, which is triggered by transfer, not by early payoff.
distractorExplanations.b: That is a late-payment charge for paying too late, the opposite of a penalty for paying off early.
distractorExplanations.d: An assumption fee applies when a buyer takes over the loan; a prepayment penalty applies to early payoff.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-m.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. It applies only when the note and applicable law allow it.

options.a: The buyer is credited; it reduces the cash needed
options.b: The seller is charged the item on the buyer's behalf
options.c: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed
options.d: The lender pays the item at closing

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the entry: a credit reduces the buyer's cash to close, while a debit is a charge that increases it.
distractorExplanations.b: A buyer debit charges the buyer; a seller-paid item would appear as a seller debit and buyer credit.
distractorExplanations.d: Lender-paid items show as credits to the buyer; a buyer debit means the buyer pays.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-m.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For the seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

options.a: Originate loans directly to borrowers at local lenders and banks
options.b: Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV loans
options.c: Set the federal funds rate that drives mortgage interest rates
options.d: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators

distractorExplanations.a: Originating loans to borrowers is the primary mortgage market; the secondary market buys those loans afterward.
distractorExplanations.b: Default insurance is the role of private mortgage insurance or FHA, not the secondary market's buying and selling.
distractorExplanations.c: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target; secondary market agencies such as Fannie Mae buy loans.

options.a: Fund construction draws on a new home and then convert to permanent financing once it is completed
options.b: Let a buyer take over the seller's existing loan at its current rate and terms
options.c: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.d: Combine a first mortgage with a second loan to avoid PMI on a low down payment

distractorExplanations.a: Describes a construction-to-permanent loan, not a short-term bridge between buying and selling homes.
distractorExplanations.b: Describes a loan assumption, which transfers an existing mortgage rather than covering a short timing gap.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a piggyback (80/10/10) loan structure used to avoid PMI, not a bridge loan.

options.a: Regulated by the FTC, not by license law
options.b: Treated as a lawful rebate that needs no written disclosure
options.c: Subject to advertising and inducement rules
options.d: Exempt from regulation when offered by the managing broker

distractorExplanations.a: State license law and its advertising rules regulate inducements by licensees, not just the FTC.
distractorExplanations.b: Even where inducements or rebates are allowed, they must be disclosed and comply with advertising rules.
distractorExplanations.d: The managing broker's status does not exempt an inducement; all licensees are bound by the inducement and advertising rules.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-il-licens.explanation: Inducements are regulated; deceptive or prohibited prizes can trigger discipline. Inducements may be restricted or require clear disclosure under state license law.

options.a: May negotiate offer terms if the supervising broker reviews and approves them afterward
options.b: Performs administrative tasks under supervision and must not negotiate unless licensed
options.c: May show property and discuss price unsupervised once trained by the firm
options.d: Performs licensed tasks under a broker's supervision without needing a license

distractorExplanations.a: Negotiating is licensed activity; after-the-fact broker approval does not let an unlicensed coordinator negotiate.
distractorExplanations.c: Showing property and discussing price are licensed activities; firm training does not replace a license.
distractorExplanations.d: Supervision does not authorize unlicensed people to perform licensed activities; only clerical tasks are allowed.

options.a: Approval of the managing broker, who controls listing terms
options.b: A new comparative market analysis supporting the revised price
options.c: Notice to the MLS and cooperating brokers before the change
options.d: Seller authorization (typically written) per the listing agreement

distractorExplanations.a: The managing broker supervises licensees but does not own the price decision; list price is the seller's call.
distractorExplanations.b: A CMA may support a price recommendation, but the seller must still authorize any change.
distractorExplanations.c: MLS notice is a reporting step after the seller authorizes a change, not the authority to make it.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-il-licens.explanation: Price is the seller's decision; agents need authority to change list price. Brokerage policy may add documentation steps.

options.a: Lawful if the seller's instruction is put in writing and signed
options.b: Illegal under federal fair housing law and typically also violates license standards
options.c: Lawful for owner-occupied homes under the single-family exemption, even with a broker
options.d: A civil matter for HUD that does not affect the broker's license

distractorExplanations.a: A written seller instruction does not make discrimination lawful; licensees must refuse discriminatory instructions.
distractorExplanations.c: The single-family owner exemption is lost when a broker or agent is used, so a licensee can never rely on it.
distractorExplanations.d: Fair housing violations are also grounds for license discipline by IDFPR, not only HUD civil action.

options.a: Wait for the next monthly reconciliation to confirm the shortage
options.b: Report it if a client files a complaint about missing funds
options.c: Close the trust account and open a new one at another bank
options.d: Immediately investigate, correct, and report/notify as required

distractorExplanations.a: Delaying until the next reconciliation leaves client funds short; a known shortage must be investigated and cured now.
distractorExplanations.b: Reporting duties do not depend on a client complaint; the broker must act and notify when the shortage is found.
distractorExplanations.c: Moving banks does not cure the shortage and may hide it; the deficit must be corrected and reported.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-il-licens.explanation: Shortages are serious; prompt remediation and required notices protect the public. Reporting and notice duties follow the state commission's trust account rules.

options.a: Permitted for any licensee because REALTOR® is a generic job title
options.b: Permitted once the licensee joins the MLS, even without association membership
options.c: A matter for the association that cannot be deceptive advertising
options.d: Improper trademark/membership misuse and can also be deceptive advertising

distractorExplanations.a: REALTOR® is a registered membership mark of the National Association of REALTORS®, not a generic job title.
distractorExplanations.b: MLS access is separate from association membership; only members may use the REALTOR® mark.
distractorExplanations.c: Misusing the mark also misleads consumers and can be deceptive advertising under state license law.

options.a: Noncompliant with brokerage identification rules
options.b: Permitted if the ad shows the licensee's license number
options.c: Permitted on social media but not in print advertising
options.d: Allowed for team ads without the firm name

distractorExplanations.b: A license number does not replace the required brokerage name; ads must identify the responsible firm.
distractorExplanations.c: Brokerage identification rules apply to online and social media ads just as they do to print.
distractorExplanations.d: Team advertising must still identify the sponsoring brokerage; a team name alone is not enough.

options.a: As brokerage income once the transaction closes, without any written disclosure to the parties
options.b: According to statutory rules (e.g., client benefit or approved housing-trust programs)
options.c: By splitting it between the listing and selling brokers at closing
options.d: By paying it to the state real estate recovery fund in every case

distractorExplanations.a: Interest on trust money is not the broker's to keep without authority; keeping it undisclosed is conversion.
distractorExplanations.c: Cooperating brokers have no claim to trust-account interest; its use is set by statute or the parties' agreement.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses trust interest with recovery-fund fees; interest goes where statute or the agreement directs, such as the client.

options.a: Comply, since the seller alone signs the disclosure form
options.b: Disclose it only if a buyer asks a direct question
options.c: Refuse to conceal legally required disclosures
options.d: Leave the defect to the home inspector

distractorExplanations.a: The licensee has an independent duty to disclose known material defects; the seller signing the form does not shift it.
distractorExplanations.b: Known material latent defects must be disclosed proactively, not only in answer to a buyer's question.
distractorExplanations.d: Relying on a buyer's inspection does not excuse concealing a known latent defect the licensee must disclose.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-il-licens.explanation: Licensees cannot participate in fraud; illegal instructions must be refused. If the seller persists, the licensee should consider withdrawing from the listing.

options.a: Full broker authority while the permanent license is processed
options.b: Limited authority until full licensing conditions are met
options.c: Authority to practice without a sponsoring broker for 90 days
options.d: Full licensure until the next renewal date

distractorExplanations.a: Provisional status is narrower, not full broker authority; broker-level rights need a broker license.
distractorExplanations.c: Provisional holders still need broker supervision; no rule allows a 90-day unsupervised practice window.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses provisional status with an active license; conditions must be met before full licensure.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-il-licens.explanation: Provisional statuses are narrower and conditioned. The scope of the limit is set by the state commission's rules.

options.a: Acceptable if the friend views it during listed showing hours
options.b: Permitted once the seller's showing service logs the entry
options.c: Allowed if the friend is pre-approved
options.d: Improper and a security/agency violation risk

distractorExplanations.a: Showing hours do not authorize access by unlicensed people; the seller's authority and security rules still apply.
distractorExplanations.b: Logging an entry is not authorization; sharing access codes with unlicensed people violates lockbox rules.
distractorExplanations.c: Loan pre-approval has nothing to do with access authority; an unlicensed person cannot be given lockbox codes.

options.a: Shifts liability for agents' violations from the broker to the agents
options.b: Documents supervision standards and compliant procedures for affiliated licensees
options.c: Takes the place of required continuing education for affiliated licensees
options.d: Satisfies the broker's supervision duty without any further review of agents' files

distractorExplanations.a: A manual does not transfer the broker's supervisory liability; the broker remains responsible for supervision.
distractorExplanations.c: Continuing education is a separate licensing requirement that a policy manual cannot replace.
distractorExplanations.d: A written manual supports but does not satisfy supervision; brokers must still actively review transactions.

options.a: Acceptable puffing if the listing includes a 'buyer to verify' note
options.b: A civil matter between the parties that is outside license law
options.c: A material misrepresentation that can trigger discipline and civil liability
options.d: A violation for the appraiser, since appraisers are the ones who measure square footage

distractorExplanations.a: A disclaimer does not cure a knowing misstatement of a measurable fact; puffing covers opinions only.
distractorExplanations.b: Knowing misrepresentation is also grounds for license discipline by IDFPR, not only a civil claim.
distractorExplanations.d: The listing licensee who knowingly advertised the false figure is responsible, whoever measures the home.
